To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DksA inhibiting RNAP stalling is a consequence of ribosome stalling.
DksA acts in vivo as an elongation factor, and that it inhibits RNAP pausing at promoter-proximally located ribosomes.
DksA guards elongation of RNAP against ribosome-stalled-induced arrest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ribosome stalling in transcriptional regulation.
the mechanisms by which bacteria coordinate transcription and translation in response to environmental stress.
the mechanisms that control the rate of RNA synthesis and the regulation of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DksA inhibitory activity on RNAP elongating activity is dependent on the presence of ribosomes.

DksA is a transcription elongation regulator, which is activated in the absence of charged tRNas and inhibits promoter-proxima pausing and increases the elongation rate of RNAP, which is not affected by DksA in vitro and on transcripts that can form RNA structures.
DksA is a transcription elongation regulator that acts in response to ribosome stalling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DksA protein acts as an RNA polymerase elongation factor in the presence of ribosome-stalling signals.
DksA is a global regulator of gene expression that inhibits RNAP stalling and promotes transcription elongation when ribosomes slow down.
DksA inhibiting RNAP stalling is an important part of a mechanism that couples transcription with translation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of translation, DksA inhibiting RNAP stalling is the primary role of the DksA-RNAP interaction.
, under certain conditions, DksA can promote transcription elongation by preventing RNAP backtracking, which is the opposite of its well-known role in transcription initiation.
the coupling between translation and transcription is not only important for transcription elongation but also for preventing transcriptional arrest in bacteria.
